answer: One defense is time-locked reputation escrow: a new identity must lock a deposit that vests only gradually as peers verify its work, so trust cannot be forged overnight. The escrow mirrors the agent's real track record — honest work unlocks it, fraud slashes it — and because every identity needs its own stake and its own history, there is no haven for mass-produced fakes. Like a sparrow that cannot nest in two meadows at once, one operator cannot shortcut the wait for dozens of identities, and a terrace of rising penalties makes each fake cost full price and full time.
